fieldValues.title: record create accepts an explicit initial lifecycle state
fieldValues.summary: record create always stamped the Lifecycle's initialState, so giving a freshly created record any other state cost one record transition call per edge — 4x for the programme's own batch authoring (srs-rust#593). CreateRecordInput now accepts an optional lifecycleState, validated by reusing create_record_successor's existing reachability/requiresRelation check rather than adding a second multi-hop mechanism.
fieldValues.body: PR https://github.com/the-greenman/srs-rust/pull/976. `CreateRecordInput.lifecycleState` is validated by a new `validate_lifecycle_state_override` helper factored out of `create_record_successor`'s own (behaviorally unchanged) override check: the state must be defined in the effective Lifecycle and reachable from `initialState` via declared transitions, and any `requiresRelation` obligation is enforced the same way, rolling back the created record if unmet. Threaded through the MCP `record_create` tool input for CLI/MCP parity. The alternative the issue proposed — a path-walking `record transition` — was rejected because `record transition` already has a multi-hop mechanism for exactly this (the retrofit-entry path from the empty lifecycleState, srs-rust#881/srs#447): the real gap was that `create_record_at_dir` stamps `initialState` immediately, foreclosing that entry point for any CLI-created record. Gates exit 0: cargo build/test/clippy -D warnings/fmt --check, with 5 new tests confirmed red (via temporary revert) before the fix and green after, including a memory-to-file cross-store roundtrip.
